arguments.content:
⚠️ **IMPORTANT: the header-only boot sweep can trash the `--resume` target mid-load (racy boot crash)**

The retention sweep exempts the resolved resume target (`_retentionBootCheck(currentSessionId: metadata?.id)`, line 462), but the *header-only* sweep right below it does not:

```dart
await _retentionBootCheck(currentSessionId: metadata?.id);
// gh-1660 boot hygiene: crashed/killed runs leave header-only session
// files behind (the clean-exit `deleteSessionIfEmpty` never ran for
// them). Fire-and-forget, best-effort — never delays the first turn.
unawaited(_sweepHeaderOnlySessions());
```

`_sweepHeaderOnlySessions()` → `cleanupEmptySessions(olderThan: 10 min)` (lib/src/session/session_repo.dart:575) soft-deletes every 1-line session file older than the grace — with **no exemption for the id this boot is about to open** (its presence row registers only after the load, so the in-repo live-presence guard doesn't cover it either).

The gap matters precisely because of what `--resume` targets: the newest folder session is a crashed header-only file whenever the last run died before producing content — and *resuming after a crash is this flag's core scenario*. Timeline when the newest session in the folder is a 1-line file with mtime > 10 min:

1. `_latestFolderSession()` resolves it (line 460).
2. `unawaited(_sweepHeaderOnlySessions())` starts walking the root concurrently with `_loadSession(metadata)`.
3. If the sweep wins, `_softDelete` moves the file to `.trash/` and `_repo.open()` then fails at the stat backstop (`Failed to read session <path>`, lib/src/session/session_storage.dart:676-684) — `_loadSession`/`run()` have no fallback, so the boot dies.

The PR description states "the boot sweeper exempts the exact resume target" — that contract currently holds only for the retention sweeper, not this one. (For `--session <name>` the exposure doesn't arise: a named session always carries a name record, so it is never header-only. `--resume` is the first path that *automatically* targets a header-only file.)

Suggested fix: thread an exempt id into `JsonlSessionRepo.cleanupEmptySessions` (skip that path during the sweep), or skip `_sweepHeaderOnlySessions()` on this boot when a resume target was resolved — the target is the newest-activity session, so deferring the sweep by one boot loses nothing.

Worst case today is bounded (one failed boot; the file is recoverable from `.trash/`; the next boot succeeds), which is why this is ⚠️ rather than 🚨 — but it should be fixed before merge.

💡 **SUGGESTION: help text says "interactive TUI mode" unconditionally, but `--resume -p "…"` composes headless**

```
--resume, --r                Start the newest session of this folder in
                             interactive TUI mode
```

`fa --resume -p "…"` is a valid, intended composition (the PR description: "Headless keeps composing … resume is not prompt-gated, so it never silently becomes interactive"), and `CliArgs.resume`'s own doc comment carries the nuance ("Interactive TUI mode when no prompt rides the invocation"). The one-line `--help` drops it, so the user-facing contract overstates the mode.

Suggested wording that fits the two-line layout:

```
--resume, --r                Start the newest session of this folder
                             (interactive TUI when no -p/--prompt is given)
```

## Review Summary — PR #2084 (`fa --resume/--r`)

**Verdict: REQUEST_CHANGES** (1 ⚠️ IMPORTANT; per policy any open ⚠️ gates approval)

The PR delivers exactly what it claims — I independently reproduced all its gates: the 7 new tests pass (83 total in the two touched files), the 4 adjacent families pass (13), `dart analyze` on the 8 touched files is clean, `dart format` reports 0 changes. The parse surface (`--resume`/`--r`, `--session` conflict error), effective-args plumbing, fresh-install exclusion, and folder-scoped boot resolution are all correct, with good doc comments and repo-convention adherence.

**The one real issue**: the boot-time **header-only sweep** (`_sweepHeaderOnlySessions`, unawaited) has no exemption for the resolved resume target — only the *retention* sweep exempts it. When the newest folder session is a crashed 1-line file older than the 10-min grace (exactly the post-crash `fa --resume` scenario the flag exists for), the sweep can soft-delete the file to `.trash/` between `_latestFolderSession()` and `_repo.open()`, and the boot dies with `Failed to read session <path>` — no fallback exists in `_loadSession`/`run()`. Bounded worst case (one failed boot, file recoverable), hence ⚠️ not 🚨, but it contradicts the PR's own "the boot sweeper exempts the exact resume target" contract.

Plus 2 💡 (reuse `SessionRepo.list(cwd:)` instead of the hand-rolled filter; `--help` wording overstates "interactive TUI mode" since `--resume -p` composes headless) and 2 🪶 digest lines. Density cap respected: 3 💡/🪶 threads ≤ 5 allowed at 176 additions.
